evidence: Turner explicitly includes Kiunthal/Kotgarhi guṇṭhī/gvṇṭhi finger under aṅguṣṭha, beside Jaunsari gūṭhā thumb. The Jaunsari/Kullui guṭhi/gathi series fits this documented western Pahari digit-name family; the survey’s central/back vowel and aspiration variation is retained. The finger-ring entry is not selected merely because some forms end in i.

Turner directly gives Oriya āṅguṭhi/āṅgṭhi/aũṭhi finger/toe under aṅguṣṭha. The Odisha/Bhatri survey aŋ(g)ṭi forms continue this digit stem with variable contraction and aspiration; the additional-k aṇḍki forms are excluded because their morphology needs separate evidence.

Turner gives Gujarati ãguṭhɔ thumb and Marathi ãgṭhī little finger/toe within aṅguṣṭha. These western survey aŋ(g)ṭi forms fit the same digit family, with source aspiration loss or simplification retained. The generic finger sense is supported by the Marathi and Oriya extension; this does not infer a ring meaning.

Turner records Kalasha hast, Western Pahari/Punjabi hatth and Nepali/Marathi hāt hand. These bare survey hand words answer the palm prompt by narrowing hand to its palm; no unexpressed tala component is added.

Turner explicitly prints Phalura hate-tāṛ, -tōṛo and -thōṛō palm of hand. The survey hatetoṛo is therefore analysed in full as inflected hand + tāḍa palm/clap, in that order; its genitive vowel is ordinary morphology, not a separate lexical node.

Turner gives Punjabi thelī palm and specifically Kotgarhi thēl paw under hastatala. The neighbouring Kullui aspirated thəl/thūl palm responses fit this contracted hand-palm family. They are not assigned indiscriminately to unaspirated tala surface.

Turner explicitly lists Bihari kewāṛī and Punjabi kavāṛ door under kavāṭa. The East Danuwar kevā̃ri and Haryanvi kuāḍ/kvāḍ responses match these regional door-panel forms, preserving nasalization and the western retroflex spelling.

Turner’s fourth branch *ḍhokka explicitly includes Nepali ḍhokā door and Kumaoni ḍhwākā gates. Majhi and Bote ḍhokā match that branch directly; unrelated dhok deception and ḍhok rock families are excluded.

Turner gives Bengali dor/duār, Nepali duwār and Kotgarhi dwār door under *duvāra. Hajong dur, Kullui dvār and Dang ḍuār fit these eastern/Pahari regional forms, with the Dang retroflex spelling retained as a phonetic qualification. The short northwestern dar forms subject to Persian influence are excluded.
